gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Sirui's own US store sells the carbon Traveler 5CX (0.92 kg, ball head) for $119 and the carbon Traveler X (0.95 kg, video head) for $99 today, so both weigh less than the Traveler 5C (about 1.05 kg, $109.90) that ChatGPT made its 'best budget' pick.
standout_why: I compared against digitalnomads.world (cited, 2026-10-17) and findingtheuniverse.com (cited, updated 2026-11-08). Digitalnomads prices four tripods. Its only Sirui is the Traveler 7C at $149.90, which it calls backordered. Findingtheuniverse gives no US prices at all, only 'Check price' links and a UK price of about £540 for the Gitzo. Neither page mentions the Traveler 5C, 5CX or X, and neither puts prices next to weights within Sirui's own range. I couldn't read amateurphotographer.com, the other cited page, because it returned HTTP 403.
decides: It changes the budget pick. On Sirui's store today, the Traveler 5CX costs $9.10 more than the 5C, weighs about 130 g less and keeps a ball head. The Traveler X costs $10.90 less and weighs about 100 g less, but it comes with a video head. ChatGPT's 5C loses to both on weight. It also changes the mid-range price: Ulanzi's own store lists the Zero Y with ball head at $279.95, not the $299.95 ChatGPT showed. That puts it $120 below Peak Design's $399.95 tripod while weighing 0.46 kg less (1.1 kg vs 1.56 kg, both from digitalnomads). Sirui is one of our affiliate programs (awin:sirui), so we can link the cheaper, lighter Sirui models directly.
